title: An operator enables an organization through an authenticated API

comments.author: home
comments.text:
As an operator (self-hosted or the private SaaS), I want to enable or suspend
an organization through an authenticated API, so that billing systems and other
external callers do not need shell access to the members CLI.

**Blocked by:** nothing. **Unblocks:** the private SaaS's Stripe webhook
handler, which becomes this API's second caller.

---
Feature: Authenticated operator enable/suspend API

  Scenario: An authenticated operator enables a pending organization
    Given an organization in pending status
    And an authenticated operator credential
    When the operator calls the enable endpoint for that organization
    Then the organization becomes enabled
    And the same state transition the members CLI produces occurs

  Scenario: An authenticated operator suspends an enabled organization
    Given an organization in enabled status
    When the operator calls the suspend endpoint for that organization
    Then the organization becomes suspended

  Scenario: An unauthenticated caller is rejected
    When a request without a valid operator credential calls the enable endpoint
    Then the request is rejected and no organization status changes

**Done when:** the members CLI is refactored to call this API path rather than
duplicating the state transition, so there is exactly one enable/suspend
implementation.

POST `/operator/orgs/{tenant_id}/{enable,suspend,reinstate}` with a deployment-wide operator bearer; empty key fail-closed; same ControlPlane transitions as the members CLI (CLI stays Dynamo-direct).
